b: I got my first credit card when I was 20. I played by the rules, never carried a balance, just used my cards for either small emergency money, and paying basic things like phone and electric bills. I've always been careful because I don't make all too much between my 2 jobs, (about 36k total), and while I've been irresponsible here and there with my money, I've been lucky enough to not have gone into any debt. After about 3 years I had gotten myself close to 800, around 790 total, and felt super accomplished.
I closed my original secured account about 6 months ago because I needed the money back from it and it only dropped about 10 points. No problem, about ~780 is still great.

Fast forward to now, six total years after opening my first card, and I've just had to carry a balance for THE FIRST TIME EVER. I had some unforeseen expenses and carried about a $1,700 balance between everything over on my statement. I owed about 30 dollars in interest. No biggie.

Then Experian sent me a nice email saying, "hey buddy, some of your credit factors changed, open the app to take a look!" I dropped to just above 730. Still decent, but you're telling me after 6 years of trying my hardest, even not eating to make sure my balance was paid off at times, and the one time I actually *USE* my credit card, *USE* the amount *YOU* gave me for something, I'm suddenly not trustworthy?

Maybe I'm overthinking or overreacting, but with all the horror stories I've heard about the credit system, it just scares me to think about what happens if this happens again another time. How much more "untrustworthy" am I going to be?
